blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Agriculture & Food Systems, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Origin, organic and deforestation-free claims face EUDR-grade scrutiny; evidence is paper and trust.
Agronomic decisions run on tradition because soil, weather and crop telemetry are patchy; input spend is uniform where it should be variable.
Harvest forecasting is regional guesswork; quality attributes (protein, moisture, defects) are discovered at intake, not predicted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: EUDR obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.
Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Contracts as production software: specification, formal verification and audit before value moves.
Proof, not paperwork: EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify.
Geolocation-anchored plots, custody events and regulator interfaces (due-diligence evidence produced continuously)
Certifications (organic, fair-trade) as verifiable credentials (premium channels unlocked with proof)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EUDR and Food-safety regimes (HACCP/EU 178/FSMA). Traceability and recall duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
